rule: Lone non-corner border cells are markers: left/right markers fix a row, top/bottom markers fix a column. Every other object containing a marker colour is rigidly translated along that single axis so that its key cell (least-frequent marker colour in the object) lies on the marker's line. Lone interior cells of a marker colour move as well. Markers and shapes without marker colours stay put, and cells pushed off the grid are dropped.
scope: Translate multicolour shapes so their least-frequent marker-coloured key aligns with the corresponding edge marker row/column. Includes lone keys, static distractors, marker-coloured bodies, paired opposite-edge markers and clipping. Random 8..30 canvases; requested 7..30. Validated against the explicitly approved corrected teaching copy.

authored_scope: Random scenes have one axis per grid: either all markers on left/right edges (vertical slides) or, by transposition, all on top/bottom edges (horizontal slides). Each scene has 1-3 marker colours on random sides, with optional duplicate markers on the opposite edge. Shapes include blobs, closed or open frames with optional interior key cells, bars and lone key cells, with optional accents. Some shapes have a body in another marker colour, which exercises the least-frequent key rule. There are static distractor shapes and lone distractor cells. About 30% of scenes allow partial off-grid clipping of moved shapes, as in test 1. Background and palette are random, and sizes range from 7 to 30 per side; defaults are 8-22 by 8-26, a modest synthetic extension beyond the fixtures. Deliberately not supported: mixed row/column axes within one grid, overlapping moved shapes, corner markers, and duplicate-colour markers on different lines (first-in-reading-order tie-break).
authored_constraints: Marker lines are interior (1..len-2), so markers are never in corners.
Lines of different marker colours are at least 2 apart, so markers never touch each other.
Each shape lives in its own column band, with at least one background column between bands, so shapes never touch (4- or 8-connected) and moved shapes never overlap.
Every input shape cell is at Chebyshev distance >= 2 from every marker, so shapes never merge with markers.
Moving shapes contain their key colour exactly once, and any other marker colour present occurs at least twice, so the least-frequent key is unique.
Static distractors and accents use only non-marker, non-background colours.
Lone cells are placed off the border rows and columns, so they are never mistaken for markers.
Every moving shape starts off its target line, so all its moves are nonzero. Each scene has at least one moving shape and at least two shapes.
Without the clip flag, moved shapes stay fully inside the grid. With it, only non-key cells may leave the grid.
Explicit scenes require markers, shapes, width, height and background together. Random-only controls are rejected for explicit scenes.
